🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-11-16 23:00 → 2026-11-17 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Commitment anchoring shipped** — the verifier can now resolve a commitment ID through an on-chain anchor instead of a trusted artifact host. [commit 117c447](https://github.com/trustless-ai/flashprove-onchain-verifier/commit/117c447bce5c3bb5df68513c0ec42f4048134501)

> **Daily rejections became explainable** — the daily pipeline now records why a draft was rejected and keeps its tone contract aligned with the output spec. [PR #17](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/17)

## 🤝 **What moved**

### flashprove-onchain-verifier
_A trust assumption moved out of the verification path and into deployed code._

- Baby Blue Viper **Proposed** an on-chain anchor for commitment IDs that replaces the trusted artifact host, giving the verifier a path to resolve commitments without depending on one hosted service. [PR #2](https://github.com/trustless-ai/flashprove-onchain-verifier/pull/2)
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Backed** that design as stronger than his own comment and merged it, keeping the review short so the better approach could land without a long debate. [tg:tawg:6403]

### ERC-8004
_A practical question about consuming validation results on-chain got a concrete answer._

- A contributor in the ERC-8004 trustless-agents thread **Clarified** that contracts can read a validation outcome because the deployed Validation Registry implementation carries it, which matters for agent designs that want on-chain checks to drive their behavior. [ERC-8004 post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8004-trustless-agents/25098/456)

### ERC-8183
_Signing for the evaluator path moved from an open question to a settled approach._

- A participant in the ERC-8183 agentic-commerce thread **Settled** the signing discussion by confirming hash-only signing inside the evaluator's call, which keeps the signed payload minimal for agentic commerce flows. [ERC-8183 post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/466)

### daily-contribution
_The daily reporting loop learned to explain its own rejections._

- Jimmy Shi **Shipped** a fix that records rejection reasons and aligns the tone output contract with the spec, so failed drafts leave behind feedback the next attempt can use. [commit a97e3f7](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/commit/a97e3f764f1322da43fd9db2cea352650f999004)

### zkIE refactor
_The rebuild moved forward with integration still in progress._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Shared** a status sync on the zkIE refactor, describing a four-layer rebuild from models through ops and engine to core split by ONNX op, which makes the overhaul legible to the group while integration continues. [tg:tawg:6405]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Whether other verifier paths can reuse the commitment-anchor pattern now that it is merged.
- Where ERC-8004 consumers will wire registry-read validation results into their agent flows.
- How the zkIE layer split will shift once ONNX op integration finishes.

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Finish the zkIE integration across the four new layers and flag any layer that needs reshaping.
- Watch the daily pipeline through a full cycle to confirm rejection reasons surface where people can see them.
- Follow the ERC-8183 thread to see whether the hash-only signing choice needs a wording update in the draft.

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** a design proposal, a fast review, and a merge took a hosted trust assumption out of the verifier in one short relay.
>
> That rhythm is worth keeping — handoffs smooth enough that the anchor barely makes a splash ⚓
